clip: Pexels, "Video of a walking horse" (https://www.pexels.com/video/video-of-a-walking-horse-9943096/): 13.9 s, 30 fps, 970x512; a saddled chestnut walking left to right (his left side to the camera), the camera panning with him for ~2 s, then holding
method: pan.py (phase correlation on the ground strip), legmask.py (legs by colour, laid on the ground: a space-time picture of the hoof band), contacts.py (stances = runs in ground columns), legs named by which leg is drawn over which as they pass (occl.jpg): the planted one is near when it hides the swinging one

scale.note: from the trunk's length (barrel + quarters ~1.6 m); +-15%

stances.note: frames at the clip's 30 fps; ground x in pixels (pan taken out); on = landing, off = the toe leaving. Frame 0 = the clip's first frame.

derived.order: LH, LF, RH, RF: the lateral sequence (as the literature)

lateral_phase.note: LH -> LF landing as a share of the stride (0.25 = evenly spaced)

derived.clip_speed: stride ~80 frames = 2.7 s at the clip's rate, at ~0.47 m/s: no walking horse is that slow; the clip is almost certainly slowed (stock is often shot at 60 fps and played at 30). At 2x the stride is 1.33 s at 0.94 m/s, at 2.5x 1.07 s at 1.17 m/s: a slow, relaxed walk either way. The clip can't say which, so timing comes from the literature and only the shares (duty, phase, poses) from the clip.

poses_by_eye.note: read off 2x crops (ang_lh.jpg, ang_lf.jpg; reference/), +-10 degrees; angles from vertical, + = hoof ahead

LF.mid_swing: knee flexed ~45, cannon ~35 back of vertical, hoof ~8-12 cm up

LH.mid_swing: hock flexed, cannon ~30 back, hoof ~10 cm up
